one_line: Sales are flat on purpose as it drops money-losing plans, and profits are recovering; the thin margin is real but improving, and legal risk remains open.

why_fell.reason: Medical costs ran far above plan in 2025, forcing guidance cuts and a CEO change.
why_fell.evidence: Hemsley returned as CEO in May 2025; management calls 2026 a transition year and expects the payoff in 2027.

why_fell.reason: Flat sales are deliberate: it is shedding unprofitable Medicare Advantage and ACA members.
why_fell.evidence: January 2026 outlook said revenue would fall about 2% to over $439 billion; Q3 revenue was $112.7 billion, down 0.4%.

why_fell.reason: Weak proposed 2027 Medicare rate hit the shares, and commercial costs still run hot.
why_fell.evidence: Shares fell as much as 15% premarket on 27 Jan 2026. Commercial cost trend is above the 11% expected, driven by arbitration payouts and specialty drugs.

why_fell.reason: Open federal criminal and civil investigations over Medicare billing.
why_fell.evidence: Company confirmed formal DOJ criminal and civil requests in July 2025; a later report said the criminal probe also covers drug management and doctor pay.

for_unfair.point: Profit is recovering fast: Q3 net profit $4.1 billion, up 75%; medical cost ratio 88.4% vs 89.9%; 2026 earnings guidance raised three times to at least $20.50 a share.
Final 2027 Medicare Advantage rate was 2.48% (about 5% with risk scores), far above the near-flat January proposal. CMS dropped the risk-model change.
Analyst targets average about $481 versus a price near $342 in the brief. Morningstar fair value was $475 (date unclear), narrow moat.

for_fair.point: Sales are really flat to falling. UnitedHealthcare expects to lose over 1 million Medicare Advantage members in 2026, and 4-plus star plan share falls from 81% to 68% for 2027.

Employer-plan costs beat expectations upward for a second straight quarter; Medicaid expected at a negative 1% margin in 2026; management says 2027 should start at the low end of its 13-16% growth target.
Legal overhang is unresolved: no 2026 ruling or charging decision found in the criminal probe or the whistleblower case; judge allowed a slimmed civil case to proceed.

what_market_fears: That medical costs keep outrunning prices, shrinking the base business for years, and that a DOJ case brings fines or limits on how it bills Medicare.
what_would_prove_it_wrong: Two quarters of falling medical cost ratio with stable sales, a good 2027 outlook in January, and the criminal probe closing without charges. Charges would prove the fear right.
next_date_to_watch: Mid-January 2027: full-year 2026 results and first 2027 outlook (exact date not found).

flag.note: Revenue is down 0.4% and guided down about 2% for 2026, so the sales half is in motion, but profit margins are rising, not falling again.

not_found: 2026 Medicare Advantage final rate (5.06% increase, April 2025 CMS) was seen only in search summary. No 2026 court or DOJ updates found. Company-stated 2026 medical cost trend figure not found. No analyst bear case from a top-tier source read. Exact Jan 2027 earnings date not found. The 2026 leadership news found was mostly from 2025.
